newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end firmer in futures-boosted trade.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end firmer in futures-boosted trade.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended firmer in busy trade on Friday, boosted by the expiry of Ibex futures which brought the index off highs just before the close.
The bourse also found strength in bond gains, as European markets apparently continue to factor in the increasing feasibility of European monetary union, dealers said.
The general index rose 0.77 points, 0.22 percent, to 358.80 and the Ibex added 11.40 points, 0.28 percent, to 4,093.60.
Hypermarket Pryca rose 60 pesetas to 3,025 after a large buy order and a put-through from a French brokerage. Some speculated on the possibility of shareholder Carrefour shifting its stake.
Electric utilities were still at the centre of trade, and most gained ground. Iberdrola reversed initial gains to end off 5 pesetas to 1,195.
Some dealers see more upside for the bourse after the 1997 budget, although uncertainties overhanging changes planned for regulated sectors still offset this to some degree.
The 1997 budget is due to be announced on September 27th.
Ahead of that, the prospect of the September 24th Federal Reserve meeting might keep a lid on trade next week, with many anticipating a hike in key U.S. rates.
